stories.headline: Carney holds firm on CUSMA review terms as US demands pre-conditions and entry fees
stories.summary: PM Carney repeatedly asserted this week that Canada will not accept US dictation of USMCA/CUSMA review terms, deny pre-negotiation concessions, and linked the provincial ban on US liquor to tariff relief. Coverage spans US demands for an 'entry fee,' Carney's 24-member advisory committee, his phone call with Mexican President Sheinbaum, and escalating rhetorical exchanges with US trade officials. Poilievre challenged Carney's approach as 'showboating,' while O'Toole praised the advisory committee as more serious than Trudeau's approach.

stories.headline: Liberals move to seize majority control of Commons committees amid opposition pushback

House Leader Steven MacKinnon defended the move as reflecting parliamentary convention.

stories.headline: Poilievre launches 'Zero Tax on Gas' tour amid growing questions about his leadership standing

stories.headline: Bank of Canada expected to hold rates steady at April 29 decision as Iran war drives energy inflation
stories.summary: Ahead of the Bank of Canada's April 29 rate announcement, economists and analysts broadly expected rates to remain at 2.25%, as energy-driven inflation from the US-Israel-Iran war conflict complicated the monetary policy outlook. Governor Macklem signalled the bank would 'look through' the short-term gasoline shock while watching for broader inflationary spillovers. The bank also appointed two new deputy governors.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada inflation and business sentiment surveys flag Iran war impact

Governor Macklem said he was not concerned about near-term inflation spikes. These results form the backdrop to the April 29 rate decision.

stories.headline: Carney Spring Fiscal Update scheduled for April 28 amid pressure to show results
stories.summary: The Carney government's first spring economic update — tabled on the one-year anniversary of the Liberal minority election win — drew pre-emptive demands from Poilievre to cap the federal deficit at $31 billion and cut major spending items. Former Parliamentary Budget Officer analysts said Carney would be under pressure to demonstrate economic results, while the Bloc Québécois submitted 11 policy proposals for the update.

stories.headline: NDP's Boulerice announces departure for Quebec provincial politics, reducing caucus to five MPs
stories.summary: Federal NDP MP Alexandre Boulerice, the last representative of the 2011 Quebec 'orange wave,' announced plans to leave federal politics to run provincially with Québec solidaire. His departure reduces the NDP caucus from six to five MPs and opens his Rosemont-La Petite-Patrie riding for a byelection that Liberals are targeting.

stories.headline: Canadian Armed Forces surpasses recruiting targets for second consecutive year
stories.summary: The Department of National Defence announced the Canadian Armed Forces enrolled 7,310 new Regular Force members in fiscal year 2025/26, exceeding its target of 6,957 and reaching the highest recruitment level in 30 years. The CAF also announced a new Digital Onboarding System for the next fiscal year.

Wiseman appeared before a parliamentary committee and apologized, but faced continued questions about his views on supply management and his ability to represent Quebec's interests.
